problem: Consider the function $f(x,y)=(x+y)\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y).$ What is the rate of change of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(2,-1)$ in the direction in which the function decreases most rapidly?

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Rate of Change of a Function in a Given Direction
examples.problem: Consider the function $g (x, y) = \ln \left(\sqrt {xy^3}\right).$ What is the rate of change of $g$ at the point $\left(\dfrac 12, \dfrac 32 \right)$ in the direction in which the function increases most rapidly?
examples.worked_solution:
At a given point, a function $g(x,y)$ increases most rapidly in the direction of its gradient at that point.

In our case, we compute $\nabla g(x,y)$ and evaluate it at the point $\left(\dfrac 12, \dfrac 32 \right)\!\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{x{y}^{3}})),\,\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{x{y}^{3}}))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{x{y}^{3}}}\cdot \frac{{y}^{3}}{2\sqrt{x{y}^{3}}},\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{x{y}^{3}}}\cdot \frac{3x{y}^{2}}{2\sqrt{x{y}^{3}}}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2x},\,\frac{3}{2y}⟩ \\ ∇g(\frac{1}{2},\frac{3}{2}) & =⟨\frac{1}{2\cdot (\frac{1}{2})},\frac{3}{2\cdot (\frac{3}{2})}⟩ \\  & =⟨1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the rate of change of $g(x,y)$ at the point $\left(\dfrac 12, \dfrac 32 \right)$ in the direction of $\nabla g\left(\dfrac 12, \dfrac 32 \right)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}‖∇g(\frac{1}{2},\frac{3}{2})‖ & =‖⟨1,1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: In what direction does the function $f(x,y)=3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y-y\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ increase most rapidly at the point $(0,1)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
At a given point, a function $f(x,y)$ increases most rapidly in the direction of its gradient at that point.

So, we compute $∇f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at the point $(0,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y-y\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y-y\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\text{ }j \\  & =(y\operatorname{sin}⁡x+6x\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\text{ }i+(3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\text{ }j \\ ∇f(0,1) & =(1\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+6\cdot 0\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(1))\text{ }i+(3(0)^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0))\text{ }j \\  & =-j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the function increases most rapidly in the direction of $-j.$
